live.name: GOLD HARVEST
live.headline: GOLD HARVEST: a threat actor tracked under several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists GOLD HARVEST under five other names and names three remote-access tools tied to it. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: The catalogue record, sourced to Secureworks, tracks the actor as GOLD HARVEST.
The same record lists these aliases: Octo Tempest, Roasted 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Scattered Spider and UNC3944.
The record lists three tools: AnyDesk, ConnectWise Control and Logmein.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: GOLD HARVEST
next.headline: GOLD HARVEST (Scattered Spider): help-desk tricks and data extortion
next.in_short: GOLD HARVEST is Secureworks' name for the actor also called Scattered Spider. Vendors describe a financially motivated group that phones help desks, steals logins and extorts victims, with blurry ties to allied groups.

sentences.t: Secureworks tracks this actor as GOLD HARVEST. The same activity is also known as Octo Tempest, Roasted 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Scattered Spider and UNC3944.
CrowdStrike describes Scattered Spider as a prolific eCrime adversary. It says the group has carried out financially motivated activity since early 2022.
CrowdStrike also lists Storm-0875 and LUCR-3 among the group's aliases.
Trustwave SpiderLabs says the Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters brand borrows the names of Scattered Spider, ShinyHunters and LAPSUS$. It reads the brand as a situational alliance, not a formal merger.

EclecticIQ analysts assess that ShinyHunters is very likely relying on members of Scattered Spider and The Com for voice phishing. The same report notes there is no direct relationship between ShinyHunters and Scattered Spider.
Resecurity says the overlaps between these groups suggest operational coordination but do not prove it.
CrowdStrike says early campaigns reportedly targeted customer relationship management and business-process outsourcing firms. It adds telecommunications and technology companies to the list.
Resecurity says the allied groups have jointly targeted financial services, technology, retail and airline organizations.
Mandiant says UNC3944 targets IT help desks to get around multifactor authentication.
Resecurity says both LAPSUS$ and Scattered Spider are known for help desk impersonation and credential theft.
A report on the wider collective lists SIM swapping, MFA fatigue and session cookie theft as ways to get past multifactor login.
Picus Labs says Scattered Spider used RustScan to probe ESXi appliances for open ports.
The catalogue record lists the remote access tools AnyDesk, ConnectWise Control and LogMeIn.

Rapid7 investigated an April 2026 intrusion that began with a Microsoft Teams message from a fake IT Support account. It says this mirrors tradecraft seen in Octo Tempest-style campaigns, and does not call it a confirmed link.
One report says ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware crippled MGM and Caesars in 2023 after a simple phone call. It says Scattered Spider acted as an affiliate.
Push says Scattered Spider made headlines again in April 2025 with attacks on UK retailers Marks & Spencer and Co-op.
Resecurity attributes ransomware attacks on WestJet, Hawaiian Airlines and Qantas in mid-2025 to Scattered Spider.
Intrinsec cites a CISA advisory of 29 July 2025 on Scattered Spider. It says the advisory names the Vidar infostealer among tools the group used.
Resecurity does not believe the alliance's announced end to operations is sincere. It expects the groups to regroup under other names.
Help desks should confirm a caller's identity through a separate, trusted channel before resetting passwords or multifactor settings.
Staff should treat unexpected chat or phone requests from "IT support" with suspicion.
